transcript:
[00:00] Sophie Martinez: Thanks everyone for joining, appreciate the time. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Priya Rao: Priya here, hi all. 
[00:10] Liam Chen: Liam, Cloud Eng.
[00:12] Amira Haddad: Amira, security.
[00:14] Ethan Park: Ethan from product.
[00:16] Sophie Martinez: Great; from Redwood Arun and Ben and me. We're gonna walk through the marketplace integration flow, reference arch and call out any blockers.
[00:25] Arun Patel: I'll start with high level—there are basically three deployment surfaces we commonly list on partner marketplaces: Redwood hosted API, Redwood Dedicated (reserved pools) and Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). For NovaMarket we talked about a marketplace listing + a reference arch for customers who want to deploy via NovaMarket's managed offering.
[00:40] Ethan Park: When you say "reference arch" is that a full deployable template or a diagram + steps?
[00:44] Arun Patel: Practically we deliver a diagram, Terraform snippets for the common pieces (VPC peering, IAM roles), and a short ops runbook. We can provide a CloudFormation/Terraform starter depending on target cloud.
[00:54] Priya Rao: Good. For the marketplace listing we need assets: product blurb, tech docs, logos, and also a pricing tile. We have a content checklist. Can Redwood share a checklist?
[01:03] Sophie Martinez: Yes, I'll share the checklist and sample pricing template after the call — link: /redwood/partner-marketplace-checklist.pdf — we'll send that in the follow up email.
[01:12] Liam Chen: On the infra side we need specifics on VPC peering, expected ports, and whether we need to set up SAML SP or redirect for SSO. Also how you handle KMS keys for customer data.
[01:24] Arun Patel: Absolutely. For VPC we typically support VPC peering and PrivateLink; we have sample security groups and required egress/ingress. For SSO we support SAML SSO (IdP initiated and SP initiated) and OIDC in some cases. KMS—we can either bring-your-own-KMS or use Redwood managed keys; for high security customers we recommend BYO-KMS with HSM-backed keys.
[01:42] Amira Haddad: For our compliance team we need SOC 2 Type II evidence, encryption at rest & in transit, and key management specs. Does Redwood have an artifacts bundle?
[01:50] Ben Torres: We do. Arun will share the compliance artifacts stub and our security pack. Some of the docs are gated but we'll send the summary pack for marketplace listing.
[01:58] Arun Patel: Note—small audio glitch—we had some customers confuse Redwood Dedicated with Redwood Dedicate, so call it Dedicated pools. Also we sometimes transcribe "KV cache" as "KV cash" in older notes, just FYI.
[02:10] Liam Chen: (laughs) Noted. On the network side, what's the typical latency footprint for the hosted API vs Dedicated? We need numbers for our performance page.
[02:18] Arun Patel: For hosted API we see p50 text-gen latencies around 70-120ms for short seqs in our benchmark region, p95 varies by model. Dedicated—because it's reserved GPU pools—we can guarantee throughput and lower tail latency, typically 20–40% better p95. We'll provide the performance profile matrix for each model variant.
[02:36] Priya Rao: For the marketplace listing, NovaMarket requires a reference architecture that includes failover and fallback options—if Redwood capacity is constrained we need to show a fallback model or strategy.
[02:46] Sophie Martinez: We have routing policies and automatic fallback to compatible model variants; we'll capture that in the reference arch.
[02:51] Ethan Park: About billing — NovaMarket needs a billing integration so customers can purchase credits or subscribe directly; does Redwood have a billing API we can integrate?
[02:59] Sophie Martinez: We have a billing contract for marketplace partners, and we expose usage reports and per-token billing exports. For the marketplace tile we can provide an expected price range and recommended SKU mapping.
[03:08] Amira Haddad: Quick security nit—how do you handle logs and PII in transcripts? We need to confirm retention controls and audit logs for private deployments.
[03:16] Arun Patel: For Private and Dedicated we support customer-managed logging with retention policies; hosted API has configurable retention and we can do no-retention (zero data retention) on enterprise plans. Audit logs and trace hooks are available via the Console; we'll include those endpoints in the doc.
[03:29] Priya Rao: Excellent. On the timeline—what's a realistic timeline for getting the listing live once we have assets?
[03:34] Ben Torres: Typical is 2–4 weeks after assets and a validated reference arch and compliance checks. If we coordinate a pilot with one reference customer it's faster.
[03:41] Liam Chen: Technical question—for Private deployment, do you provide an on-prem appliance or do we run Redwood as containers in our infra?
[03:46] Arun Patel: We ship a customer package that runs as containers in customer infra (K8s) or an air-gapped bundle for on-prem. There's also a VPC-hosted private option where control plane is still Redwood but data plane is in your VPC.
[03:58] Ethan Park: For the marketplace listing we also want a quick-start demo that shows provisioning via NovaMarket. Is there a demo app or SDK we can use?
[04:04] Sophie Martinez: Yes, we'll share a reference app and a short video demo. Link placeholder: /redwood/reference-apps/marketplace-demo.zip
[04:11] Priya Rao: Are there any lock-up agreements or exclusivity clauses we should be aware of?
[04:15] Sophie Martinez: Not for standard marketplace partnerships. Commercial terms can be negotiated but nothing compulsory for listing.
[04:20] Amira Haddad: Back to compliance—can you confirm the KMS flow for BYO keys? Do you use customer-wrapped keys or do you accept key policies via IAM?
[04:28] Arun Patel: We integrate with customer KMS by referencing ARNs and support envelope encryption; for HSM-backed customers we have a recommended approach documented—we'll share the KMS integration notes.
[04:36] Liam Chen: For the staging tests, what logs or telemetry should we capture so Redwood engineers can help debug performance?
[04:41] Arun Patel: Request traces (trace id), model variant, sequence length, tokenization samples, and KV cache hit rates. We'll give a small script to run synthetic load and gather these metrics.
[04:51] Sophie Martinez: Sounds like we have concrete action items. Any other questions?
[04:55] Ethan Park: One ask—can you include a short section in the reference arch about multi-tenant isolation and how you do per-tenant quotas? We need to show that for enterprise customers.
[05:03] Arun Patel: Yes, we'll include per-tenant quota examples and rate-limiting configs. Also will show how we do cost attribution per token.
[05:12] Priya Rao: Great. If all good, we'll aim to have our content owners produce assets by Nov 3 and engineering to hand staging details by Nov 4.
[05:20] Sophie Martinez: Perfect. We'll send the checklist and draft architecture by Nov 5.
[05:24] Amira Haddad: One more—audit window for logs? We sometimes need 12–24 months. Can Redwood support extended retention for marketplace customers?
[05:31] Ben Torres: Yes, extended retention is an add-on. We'll include retention tiers in the pricing/ops doc.
[05:37] Liam Chen: Great, that's all from infra side.
[05:40] Sophie Martinez: Thanks everyone — we'll recap next steps in email. Meeting end.
